description: Synthetic answer-intent dev set (strand sira-intent). Topics follow the public operator plans used locally (attach and data retry, SMS over IMS, band 13 access, OTA device management); wording is authored, not taken from user traffic. Query text only, no corpus content, placeholder requirement IDs, no real plan codes, no real operator codes, fictitious release labels. Operator codes are written as {MNO_A}/{MNO_B}/{MNO_C} and filled in at load time from the analyzer's alias table. Labels are authored from human-read intent, NOT from rule output. 10 samples per intent.
labelling_rules: One label per question: the answer shape the asker most wants.

change: what moved between releases or versions of ONE operator's documents. A change question that asks for a list ('list the requirements that changed') is still change, because it routes to History.
compare: two or more things side by side (operators, plans, features, or an operator against a standard). Two operators asking 'what changed' is compare, never change.

compliance: whether a described behaviour or implementation meets the requirements. A yes/no about what the spec itself says ('is T3402 reset at power off?') is fact. A pasted bug report asking for a verdict ('is this bug valid?', 'can you comment on this issue?', 'expected X but it does Y') is compliance, even when it mentions a release or a change.
list: every item of a kind. explain: how, why, overview, summary. fact: one value or one statement.
other: none of the above (greetings, bare keywords, requests the system does not serve).
